name: Dockside IsoKnit Cryo-Handler Glove
description:
Bulky mid-forearm gloves in a dense recycled-wool outer shell over a closed-cell neoprene insulation layer, then a vapor-barrier liner in silver mylar. The exterior is a salt-stained cream-grey with orange reflective stripe at the cuff. Built for cold-chain dock work in the Lake Meridian corridor — sustained sub-zero handling of cryo-containers and refrigerated freight.

The right glove features a cutaway thumb and index for scanner-pad operation without full removal. Wrist strap is adjustable and rated for tether-clip attachment. Chrome-arm users get an extended cuff with a ratchet closure that seals over prosthetic wrist housings.
functionality: Rated to -40°C sustained contact. Vapor-barrier liner prevents moisture ingress from cryo-containers. Cutaway right thumb and index allow scanner-pad operation. Chrome-arm extended cuff with ratchet closure seals over prosthetic wrist housings. Tether-clip wrist strap rated to 80kg load.
what_it_says: Cold-dock labor — unglamorous, essential, and hard on the body whether you've still got both original hands or not.
story_hooks: A cryo-container flagged as machine parts contains something biological — and the dock worker who handled it is now running a fever no med-patch can identify.
The ratchet cuff design was copied from a military cold-weather augment spec without licensing; a corponation legal team has arrived at the docks.
A veteran dock worker with two chrome arms has worn the same pair for six years — the mylar liner has a hand-drawn map of the port's blind spots on the inside.
